newsitem.title: PERU: Savage loses Peru's Mahr bid.
newsitem.headline: Savage loses Peru's Mahr bid.

text.p: Savage Resources Ltd lost its bid for Peruvian state-owned miner Mahr Tunel to Peru's Volcan, which paid U$127 million and a investment commitment of at least $60 million over five years.

Volcan, a mid-sized company, beat the $61 million offer from Savage Resources Ltd and Peru's Morococha, and an $85 million offer from Sweden's Boliden. Both those bidders also offered investment of more than $60 million.
Volcan's stock soared 10 percent on the Lima bolsa to 14.99 by 11.15 local (1615 GMT), while Morococha's price slipped 10 percent to 7.65 soles at the same time.
State miner Centromin, which owned Mahr Tunel, had set a $50 million minimum bid price and a minimum investment commitment of $60 million over five years.
The Mahr Tunel SA unit controls the San Cristobal and Andaychagua mines, which lie close to each other in the central Peruvian highlands.
Last year, San Cristobal produced 680,000 dry tonnes of ore containing zinc, lead, copper and silver, while Andaychagua produced about 395,000 dry tonnes of ore with silver, lead and zinc.
Volcan said it might start looking for a partnership with a foreign company.
"We are holding discussions, and approaching (other mining companies) but for the moment there is nothing decisive," said Eduardo Llosa, general manager of Volcan, after Friday's sale.
Market sources said they believed the call for a partnership was a sign the company might not be able to pay what it has promised.
